providers.description: OYO (Oravel Stays Limited) is an India-headquartered hospitality company that operates a franchise and aggregator platform for budget and mid-market hotels, homes, and vacation rentals across India, Southeast Asia, Europe, and other markets. Founded in 2013 by Ritesh Agarwal and backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, OYO standardizes independent properties under its brands and distributes them through its consumer apps and website. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector company; as of this enrichment pass OYO publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Pepperfry
providers.description: Pepperfry is an Indian online marketplace for furniture and home products, founded in 2011 and headquartered in Mumbai. It sells furniture, decor, lamps, kitchen and dining goods, furnishings, and modular home solutions to consumers across India through its website, mobile apps, and a network of physical studio showrooms. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/GraphQL specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface: the consumer site is fully bot-protected (HTTP 403) and there is no evidence of an externally documented API program. The one artifact captured is a live domain-security probe of pepperfry.com.

providers.name: PriceBaba
providers.description: PriceBaba is an India-based consumer price-comparison and gadget research platform, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Mumbai. It helps shoppers compare mobile phones, consumer electronics and other gadgets by aggregating specifications, expert and user reviews, and prices across online and offline local retail stores, so buyers can find the best available deal near them. PriceBaba is backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups). No public developer program or API surface was discoverable during this enrichment pass. The website is served behind Cloudflare and blocks automated access, and no api.pricebaba.com host resolves.

providers.name: QikPod
providers.description: QikPod was an Accel-backed Indian startup that built an automated parcel locker network for last-mile e-commerce delivery, letting shoppers collect and return packages from unattended smart lockers placed in apartments, offices, and retail locations. The company has since rebranded and pivoted to Leapmile Robotics, a nano-warehouse automation and intelligent fulfillment platform that uses robotics to handle storage, retrieval, picking, auditing, and dispatch inside compact autonomous warehouse facilities. The legacy qikpod.com domain now redirects to leapmile.com/qikpod. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead; no public developer API surface has been found for either the QikPod or Leapmile properties.

providers.name: S4S Technologies
providers.description: S4S Technologies operates what it describes as India's only full-stack food processing platform, running tech-driven farm-gate procurement and processing for the food and beverage industry. The company sources fresh produce from farmers through Village Level Collection Centres, processes it through climate-clean micro food-processing units, and supplies convenience-driven ingredients (fruits, vegetables, pulses, grains, and spices) to more than 1,100 food and beverage customers. It is a B2B agritech and food-supply-chain business rather than a software or API provider; no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Samunnati
providers.description: Samunnati is an integrated agri-enterprise platform working to de-fragment India's agricultural value chain by connecting farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), and agri enterprises. It combines financial solutions (lending to farmers, FPOs, and agri businesses), trade facilitation and market linkages, and digital marketplaces (FPO Next, Trade Next, and input, output, credit, and consumer marketplaces), alongside innovation, research, and foundation-led community work. Operating across Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Jaipur, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar, it positions itself as one of India's largest agri enterprises. Samunnati runs several customer-facing digital platforms but does not publish a public developer portal or API at this time.

providers.name: Sheroes
providers.description: Sheroes is a women-only social network and community platform based in India, founded in 2014 by Sairee Chahal. It gives women a safe, moderated space to connect, ask questions anonymously, seek support, learn, and grow across communities spanning careers, health, relationships, parenting, entrepreneurship, and personal finance. The platform operates a mobile app and website, offers helpline and expert support, and has expanded into women-focused financial services (MahilaMoney). Sheroes was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Sheroes exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or documented event/webhook surface; the site is a fully client-side single-page application. This profile therefore captures the company identity plus a live domain-security probe of its public host.

providers.name: Shriram City
providers.description: Shriram City (Shriram City Union Finance Ltd) was a leading Indian non-banking financial company (NBFC) in the Shriram Group, offering personal, business, two-wheeler, gold and small-enterprise loans plus fixed deposits. Founded 1986 in Chennai, it was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners. In November 2022 the company was amalgamated into Shriram Finance Ltd; its www.shriramcity.in host no longer resolves and the shriramcity.in apex now redirects to shriramfinance.in. No public developer or API program was found. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline: web search + live domain/security/well-known probes.

providers.name: Silagroup
providers.description: SILA is a next-generation business services and real estate platform based in India, backed by Norwest Venture Partners. It delivers strategic solutions across Facility Management, Material Handling Services, Food & Catering, Real Estate Advisory, and Real Estate Development, supporting corporate entities, real estate funds, landowners, and developers throughout the entire real estate lifecycle. SILA runs a WordPress-based corporate website (silagroup.co.in) and publishes no public developer API surface; the only exposed HTTP API is the internal WordPress REST (wp-json) endpoint used to render the CMS. Enrichment confirmed no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, no /.well-known discovery documents, and no developer portal, SDKs, or docs as of this pass.

providers.name: simsim
providers.description: simsim was an Accel-backed India-based social / video commerce startup (sector: consumer) that let creators sell products through short shoppable videos; it was acquired by Google in 2021 and wound down. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-21 confirm the simsim.in zone is live for email only (Google Workspace MX + SPF), with no resolving web host (apex or www), no api/app/developer/docs subdomains, and no reachable HTTPS, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: SK Finance Ltd
providers.description: SK Finance Ltd (skfin.in) is a Jaipur, India-based non-banking financial company (NBFC) providing asset-backed retail lending. Its products span commercial vehicle, car, tractor, construction-equipment and two-wheeler loans alongside secured business loans and home-renovation / mortgage finance, delivered through a physical branch network with EMI calculators, online EMI payment, a branch locator, a loan-application portal and a customer "Refer and Earn" referral program. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate/marketing website (Next.js) with no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or other machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Spenny
providers.description: Spenny is an Indian personal-finance and micro-investing app that works like a digital piggy bank, rounding up everyday spending on cards, UPI, and netbanking and automatically investing the spare change. Users can put round-ups and lump sums (from as little as Rs. 10) into digital gold and curated mutual fund baskets, with no lock-ins and anytime withdrawals. Spenny is a consumer mobile application and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: StalkBuyLove
providers.description: StalkBuyLove was an India-based online women's fashion e-commerce retailer, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the brand appears defunct as an independent property, since the stalkbuylove.com domain now returns a 301 permanent redirect to styched.in (Styched, an unrelated Shopify-powered Indian youth-fashion retailer). No public developer portal, API, SDK, MCP server, changelog, or other machine-readable API surface could be found for StalkBuyLove on any registry or well-known path. The only honest signal available is the domain, DNS, and TLS security posture of the redirecting host, captured in the domain-security artifact.

providers.name: SwitchMe
providers.description: SwitchMe was a Mumbai, India based fintech startup founded in 2012 and backed by 500 Global that helped consumers evaluate and switch their home loans and mobile service providers, handling document collection and submission on their behalf. The company appears to be defunct: no public developer program, API, or documentation could be found, and its switchme.in domain currently resolves to unrelated content. This profile records what could be verified during the enrichment pass; there is no API surface to catalog at this time.

providers.name: Taggle Internet Ventures
providers.description: Taggle Internet Ventures Private Limited was an Indian online group-buying / daily-deals platform (taggle.com) incorporated in 2010 in Bangalore, Karnataka, that brought consumers together to purchase discounted products and services from merchants across food & beverage, wellness, and beauty. It raised an early venture round in 2010 and is now reported as permanently closed. The enrichment pass found no live developer program, public API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or documentation for this entity. Note: the taggle.com domain is now operated by an unrelated Australian digital water-metering company, Taggle Systems, which is a distinct company and not the subject of this record. This profile was surfaced during VC-portfolio mining and is retained as a historical/closed-company stub with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Tapchief
providers.description: Tapchief was an India-based online marketplace that connected businesses and professionals with a vetted network of freelance experts, consultants, and advisors for project-based work, on-demand consultations, and expert advice. Founded in Bengaluru and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), the platform let companies discover, book, and collaborate with independent talent across functions such as marketing, finance, product, and technology. Tapchief was acquired by Chargebee in 2021, and the tapchief.com domain is now dormant. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; probing found no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Three Wheels United
providers.description: Three Wheels United is a fintech-driven electric vehicle financing company in India, founded in 2017 by Cedrick Tandong, Kevin Wervenbos, and Apurv Mehra. It works to remove the financial barriers to clean mobility by providing loans for two- and three-wheeler electric vehicles — starting with auto-rickshaws — disbursed through its RBI-registered NBFC lending partner Shabri Investments Private Limited. The company pairs credit with a mobile app that helps drivers manage their loans and connect to services, and reports over 4,000 vehicles financed, 20,000+ customers served, and thousands of tonnes of CO2 reduced across Bangalore, Mumbai, and the Delhi NCR (Noida) region. It is backed by Techstars, Delta Corp Holdings, Asian Development Bank Ventures, Microsoft, and other global investors, having raised roughly $10 million in Series A funding. It is a consumer-facing lender with no public developer program, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: Toolsvilla
providers.description: Toolsvilla is an India-based e-commerce marketplace for machinery, tools, and equipment, positioning itself as one of India's largest online stores for industrial, agricultural, and power tools serving small businesses, farmers, and trade buyers. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer API, documentation, or SDKs were found during this enrichment pass; the site's internal backend at api.toolsvilla.com is undocumented and returns a bare JSON response.

providers.name: Virgio
providers.description: Virgio is an India-based direct-to-consumer sustainable fashion brand delivering trend-driven, eco-conscious womens apparel built around circular fashion, recycled and natural fabrics (recycled polyester, organic cotton, viscose, modal, lyocell), ethical production, and zero-waste packaging. It operates as an online-first retail marketplace with a consumer web storefront and mobile app. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Prosus Ventures; an enrichment probe found a consumer e-commerce presence but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: ZipDial
providers.description: ZipDial was a Bangalore, India based mobile marketing and analytics startup founded in 2010 that pioneered "missed call" engagement, letting consumers interact with brands and campaigns by giving a toll-free number a missed call rather than paying for a call or SMS. It was acquired by Twitter in January 2015 and its standalone product was subsequently wound down. The company was backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) among other investors. As of this enrichment pass the original company is defunct and no longer operates a developer program or public API; the zipdial.com domain now resolves to an unrelated general-interest content/news aggregation site with no developer, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Dunzo
providers.description: Dunzo was an Indian hyperlocal delivery and quick-commerce platform founded in July 2014 in Bengaluru by Kabeer Biswas, Ankur Agarwal, Dalvir Suri and Mukund Jha, which grew from a WhatsApp group into an app-based service delivering groceries, food, medicines, pet supplies and same-city packages across up to nine Indian cities. Its Dunzo for Business (D4B) offering gave merchants last-mile delivery through a partner API and through multi-carrier aggregators. Backed by Google, Blume Ventures, Alteria Capital and Reliance Retail, the company was dissolved on 14 January 2025; the app and website were shut down and every Dunzo-operated host, including its merchant API, is now offline. This profile is retained as a historical record — Dunzo publishes no developer portal, documentation, specification or support channel today.

providers.name: Getsupp
providers.description: Getsupp was an India-based digital health and wellness platform offering supplement and nutrition product discovery, personalized health recommendations, and online consultations with certified experts (nutritionists, dietitians, and coaches). The company was a General Catalyst portfolio company and was subsequently absorbed into Eka.care. As of this enrichment pass the getsupp.in and getsupp.com domains no longer serve a standalone site: both resolve to Eka.io infrastructure (65.0.57.69, TLS cert altnames *.eka.io) and return HTTP 404 for all paths. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, /.well-known/ discovery, or /llms.txt could be found. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead with no enrichable API surface.

providers.name: Mochatrade
providers.description: Mochatrade is a regulated neo-brokerage for Indian traders offering onchain perpetual futures on US stocks and commodities. Traders access 50+ US equities (including TSLA, NVDA, AAPL), pre-IPO names, commodities, and crypto with up to 20x leverage, settled in USDC on Hyperliquid, with INR on- and off-ramps via UPI and self-custody wallets. Founded in 2026 by IIT graduates who previously built a crypto wallet acquired after 2M installs, the company brings professional-grade derivatives execution to India's 140M+ demat account holders. Backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and Pioneer. As of this enrichment pass Mochatrade publishes only a marketing landing page (a client-rendered SPA) and no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Redcarpetup
providers.description: Redcarpetup is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of y-combinator and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

bands.label: Not Yet Rated
bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

providers.name: Battery Smart
providers.description: Battery Smart is India's largest battery-swapping network for electric two- and three-wheelers, founded in 2019 by Pulkit Khurana and Siddharth Sikka and operated from New Delhi by Upgrid Solutions Private Limited and Upgrid Electrilease Private Limited. It runs an asset-light, partner-led model: local businesses — kirana stores, petrol pumps and neighbourhood shops — host swap points where a driver exchanges a depleted lithium-ion pack for a charged one in roughly two minutes and pays per swap instead of buying the battery with the vehicle, which removes the single largest cost from an electric two- or three-wheeler. The network is concentrated in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Jaipur and Lucknow, and the company has raised across eleven rounds including a USD 65 million Series B led by LeapFrog Investments with MUFG Bank, Panasonic, Ecosystem Integrity Fund, Blume Ventures and British International Investment participating, plus a USD 15 million debt round with Mirova in April 2026. Battery Smart's software ships only as end-user Android applications — Battery Smart Driver and Battery Smart Partner — backed by a production API host at api.upgrid.in that self-identifies as the "Battery Smart API". As of this profile the company publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Norwest Venture Partners
providers.description: Norwest Venture Partners is a multi-stage venture capital and growth equity investment firm founded in 1961 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with additional presence in San Francisco and subsidiaries in Mumbai, India and Tel Aviv, Israel. As of its 2024 NVP XVII fund ($3B), the firm manages more than $15.5 billion in capital and has backed over 700 companies across its history. Norwest invests across the full lifecycle — from early-stage venture through late-stage growth equity — with sector focus spanning enterprise and B2B SaaS, cloud and infrastructure, AI, fintech, healthcare and life sciences (including biotech and digital health), and consumer and lifestyle brands. The firm is known for a hands-on but non-intrusive partnership model, backing its founders with Portfolio Success programs across talent, operations, leadership, and go-to-market. Notable investments include Plaid, Uber, Spotify, Opendoor, Gong, Vuori, Kendra Scott, Casper, Udemy, Avetta, Adaptive Insights, YipitData, Babylist, Workato, and Veza.

providers.name: Prosus Ventures
providers.description: Prosus Ventures is the venture-capital arm of Prosus, the Amsterdam-headquartered global consumer-internet and technology group (part of the Naspers group), founded in 2015 to make early-stage and growth-stage technology investments in high-growth markets outside the United States and China. The firm invests to "fuel the ecommerce flywheel," backing companies across food delivery, fintech, consumer services, logistics, e-commerce and marketplaces, plus a strong and growing focus on early-stage AI startups that reshape the e-commerce value chain (shopping and advertising tech, customer support, AI agents and operations) and frontier technologies such as quantum computing, robotics, space and biotech. Prosus Ventures typically invests from seed through Series B and into growth rounds, with a primary geographic focus on India, Latin America and Europe, plus activity in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and ANZ. In fiscal year 2025 the group committed and invested over $400 million across 40+ closed transactions, including roughly $88 million into AI. Its public portfolio spans 80+ companies including Meesho, Urban Company, PharmEasy, Klar, ElasticRun, BandLab, Ema, Corti and Oxford Ionics. The venture team is led by CEO Martin Tschopp with regional heads across India, Europe, Southeast Asia and the Middle East.
